nodes.text: to take a great burning stake and blind you.
Cario
And I'll play Circe, the one who stirs up the drugs,
who once in Corinth persuaded the companions of Philonides,
as though they were boars,
to eat kneaded dung, and she kneaded it for them herself;
I'll imitate her in every way;
and you, grunting with delight,
a little way off from the head of some old woman,
which I had a fiendish longing to creep up to.
Then, looking up, I see the priest
snatching the cakes and the dried figs
off the holy table; and after this
he went round all the altars in a circle,
in case a flat-cake had been left anywhere;
then he consecrated these into a sort of sack.
And I, thinking there was great piety in the practice,
get up and go for the pot of porridge.
Through my little cloak;
for it had holes, and not a few, by Zeus.
And first of all, for Neocleides, a plaster
medicine he set about grinding, throwing in
three heads of Tenian garlic. Then he pounded [them]
in the mortar, mixing in with them sap
and mastic; then, soaking it in Sphettian vinegar,
he plastered his eyelids, turning them inside out, so that
he would feel more pain. And he, screaming and bawling,
